chunks: Al-Muthannā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Ḥakam, who said:
I said to a servant of ours, “Prepare our meal for us.” So he took for us some of the birds of Mecca, slaughtered them, and cooked them.
Then I entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he said: “Bury them, and offer fidyah for each bird among them.”

key_terms.أَطْيَارِ مَكَّةَ: birds belonging to or found in the sanctuary area of Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on slaughtering birds from the sanctuary of Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning birds taken from the sanctuary area of Mecca. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام instructs that the cooked birds are not to be eaten, but buried, and that compensation must be paid for each bird, indicating the sanctity of the Haram and the prohibition of such hunting.
